A.biggest_strength: Unified, intuitive interactivity: clicking any array cell or stepping through comparisons updates the array pointers, plain-English trace, highlighted line of code, and spatial candidate-halving funnel in lockstep, paired with an interactive log-scale halving ladder up to n = 1,000,000,000.
A.biggest_weakness: Does not discuss practical implementation edge cases such as duplicate elements (finding the first match) or integer overflow in (lo + hi) / 2 in fixed-width integer languages.

B.biggest_strength: The supplementary reference tables below the figure concisely cover practical engineering nuances (integer overflow in low + high, duplicate values/lower bound, and half-open intervals), and the SVG pointers clearly show the comparison expression right above mid.
B.biggest_weakness: Confusing dual navigation (5 scenes vs. 7–9 steps) and visual layout collisions: Scene 5 hides the array while leaving the 16-cell range ladder orphaned below the purple bar chart, and on mobile the scene labels disappear and the TARGET badge overlaps the range ladder.
factual_errors: In Scene 5 ('Why log2 n'), the headline equation states n / 2^k >= 1 => k <= log2(n) (which evaluates to k <= 4 for n = 16) directly above a bar chart showing 5 max compares for n = 16, omitting the +1 from the main displayed formula (which is only mentioned in the tiny corner readout and bottom notes).

structured_output.reasons: Page A better serves a blog post reader by pairing a clear, single-timeline interactive binary search trace (with clickable array cells, live code-line highlighting, and a spatially aligned candidate funnel) with a second interactive halving ladder that lets the reader scale n from 1 to 1,000,000,000. Page B splits navigation awkwardly between 5 scenes and a separate step scrubber, hides the step-by-step explanation in tiny 10.5px corner text, leaves the 16-cell range ladder orphaned below the Scene 5 bar chart when the array fades out, and suffers from overlapping elements and hidden button labels at phone width.
